correctness.rationale: For n>=3,a>=1, the exact 2^n halfspace inequalities define the one-sided stretched cross-polytope. The candidate John parameters from the positive root of (n+1)c²+[2na/(a-1)-(a-1)]c-a=0 give b²=(a-c)(1+c)/n, r²=[1-2c/(a-1)]/(n-1); both facet classes are at support 1. Normalized facet contacts with orbit masses (a-c)/(a+1) and (1+c)/(a+1) have zero mean and covariance I/n, proving global John optimality. For the outer ellipsoid, two explicit branches separated at a*=(n+1)/(n-1) contain every vertex and admit nonnegative isotropic contact designs; in the second branch the -e1 pole lies strictly inside. Their log volume derivatives match at a*, but second derivative jumps by (n-1)^3/[4n(n+1)]; semiaxis limits establish the volume ratio. Independently recalculated facet and vertex support equalities across n=3,4,7 and five a values each; exact contact identities in the proof, not finite examples, certify unrestricted global uniqueness.
